name: First Aid Level 1
audience: Appointed workplace first aiders
Safety representatives and supervisors
Employees who want first aid certification
Anyone who wants to respond to emergencies at work

faqs.q: How much does First Aid Level 1 cost?
faqs.a: First Aid Level 1 costs R650 per person and runs over one day. Classes run daily, so there is no waiting period to book. The price is negotiable for group bookings, and we also offer training on site at client premises. To book a seat or get a group quote, email us at info@rehtraining.co.za.

faqs.q: Do I need any experience before doing First Aid Level 1?
faqs.a: No, you do not need previous first aid experience or a medical background to do First Aid Level 1. The course starts with the basics, including scene safety, casualty assessment and basic life support, and builds up from there. It suits anyone who wants to act as a workplace first aider or simply be ready to help in an emergency.

faqs.q: How long is the First Aid Level 1 certificate valid?
faqs.a: Certificates are issued in line with the SAQA-aligned unit standard for this course. Most workplaces set their own refresher schedule, often every few years, so check your organisation's policy or ask our team when you book. We can also arrange refresher training at your premises. Email us at info@rehtraining.co.za for details.

faqs.q: Can you train at our site?
faqs.a: Yes, we run on-site training at client premises anywhere in South Africa, or you can attend at our centres in Midrand (14 Douglas Road, Glen Austin) or Durban (62 Lilian Ngoyi Street, Windermere). On-site training works well for groups of staff who all need first aid certification. Contact us on email info@rehtraining.co.za or call 010 746 6954 to arrange a date.

name: First Aid Level 2
audience: Appointed workplace first aiders
Safety representatives and team leaders
Employees who need level 2 certification for their workplace
Staff in higher-risk work environments

faqs.q: What is the difference between First Aid Level 1 and Level 2?
faqs.a: First Aid Level 2 builds on Level 1 and goes further into workplace requirements, prioritising treatment and managing medical emergencies. It is aligned to unit standard 120496, while Level 1 is aligned to 119567. Both cost R650 and run over one day. If you are not sure which level your workplace needs, email us at info@rehtraining.co.za and we will advise you.

faqs.q: How much does First Aid Level 2 cost?
faqs.a: First Aid Level 2 costs R650 per person and runs over one day. Daily classes mean you can book without waiting, and prices are negotiable for group bookings. Training is available at our Midrand and Durban centres or on site at client premises. Email us 061 580 7967 or call 010 746 6954 to book.

faqs.q: Can I do First Aid Level 2 without Level 1?
faqs.a: You can, but Level 2 assumes the basics covered in Level 1, so most learners do Level 1 first. The course covers workplace requirements, scene assessment, basic life support and treatment of injuries and medical emergencies. If your employer requires a specific level, confirm it before booking, or ask us on email info@rehtraining.co.za and we will help you choose.

faqs.q: How long does the course take and where does it run?
faqs.a: First Aid Level 2 runs over one day with daily classes, so you can book without a waiting period. Training takes place at our Midrand or Durban centres, or on site at your premises for groups. The price is R650 per person and negotiable for group bookings. Email us at info@rehtraining.co.za to book.

name: Emergency Evacuation Procedures
description: This course covers the practical side of emergency evacuations in the workplace. Learners are taught how evacuation plans work, how to read and apply evacuation routes and assembly points, and what their role is during an emergency. The training covers fire and other emergency scenarios, how to assist visitors and people with limited mobility, and how to support an orderly evacuation without panic. On completing the course, learners can take part in and help coordinate safe evacuations and contribute to their workplace emergency plan.
outcomes: Explain emergency evacuation plans, routes and assembly points
Respond correctly during fire and other emergency evacuations
Assist colleagues, visitors and people with limited mobility to evacuate safely
Support the roll call and reporting process after an evacuation
Identify where evacuation procedures fit into workplace safety compliance
audience: All employees in workplaces with evacuation plans
Safety representatives and supervisors
Reception, security and front of house staff
Anyone responsible for emergency preparedness

faqs.q: How much does the Emergency Evacuation Procedures course cost?

faqs.a: Yes, we train on site at client premises anywhere in South Africa, or at our centres in Midrand (14 Douglas Road, Glen Austin) and Durban (62 Lilian Ngoyi Street, Windermere). faqs.q: What does a fire marshal do?
faqs.a: A fire marshal, also called a fire warden, helps keep the workplace safe from fire. Duties include spotting fire hazards, supporting evacuation procedures, assisting occupants during an emergency and using firefighting equipment within its limits. This course covers those duties in full. Call 010 746 6954 or email info@rehtraining.co.za to book.

faqs.q: Who should attend the Fire Marshal course?
faqs.a: The course is for appointed fire marshals and fire wardens, safety officers and supervisors who support workplace fire safety. No previous fire training is needed, though it helps to know your building's layout and procedures. You can train at our Midrand or Durban centres, or on site at your premises. Email info@rehtraining.co.za.

faqs.q: Can you train at our site?
faqs.a: Yes, we run Fire Marshal training on site at client premises, which lets your marshals practise with your own alarms, exits and assembly points. We also offer centre-based training in Midrand and Durban. Daily classes mean you can start soon. Contact us on email info@rehtraining.co.za or call 010 746 6954.
